How do I contact support or open a ticket?

Open NOSHX, choose TICKETS, then NEW TICKET. Give it a subject, a topic and a priority, and describe what happened; the app version and platform are attached unless you untick them. Support replies in the same thread, and you are emailed when they do. Tickets are private to you and NOSHASHI support, and you need to be signed in. From the Support chat, OPEN A TICKET WITH SUPPORT carries your question into a new ticket. Never paste a secret key or seed: a ticket that contains one is refused before it is sent.

How do I learn to use NOSHASHI?

Open LEARN and choose Hands-on labs. Each lab takes you through a real screen: TAKE ME TO opens it with a real mainnet address or token already filled in, the step says what to look for, and one question checks what you saw. Every question you answer right joins your review deck and comes back a day later, then after 3, 7, 16 and 35 days; a missed one comes back tomorrow. REVIEW on the Labs page shows what is due. There are seven labs: checking an address, NFT rights, the inbox, the verification gate, ledger sync, NOSHX, and multi-signature treasuries (that one needs Pro for its screen). Progress is kept on this device.

How do I give an examiner or regulator access?

In an organization on Institutional or above, an owner, admin or compliance member opens POLICY › MEMBERS › REGULATOR SEATS, enters the examiner's email (they need their own NOSHASHI account) and chooses 7, 30, 90 or 180 days. The examiner can read the organization's policies, exceptions, investigations and audit trail and cannot change anything. The seat ends on its date without anyone acting, can be revoked at any time, and every visit the examiner makes is written to the audit trail.

How do I monitor my book on a schedule and set my own alerts?

Open PORTFOLIO & RADAR › MONITOR (Institutional). Turn the schedule on, choose every 1, 4, 6, 12 or 24 hours and a scenario, and every wallet in the book is stress-tested with the same model as the Risk screen while the app is open. Under ALERT RULES, create a rule from conditions such as recovery ratio below 60% or freezable share above 25%, joined by ALL or ANY, for every wallet or chosen ones, and send it to the console, a desktop notification or your organization's webhooks (event custom_alert). Runs and alerts are recorded in the organization's audit log.

How do I screen deposits before crediting them?

Open ADJUDICATION › LEDGER WATCH (Enterprise). Paste the transaction hash and your deposit address, set your accepted issuers, deny list, whether a destination tag is required and your Travel Rule threshold, and press SCREEN. NOSHASHI reads the payment live: it credits what actually arrived (never the Amount of a partial payment), holds a familiar ticker whose issuer owes nothing as counterfeit, flags dust carrying a link as phishing, and traces who funded the sender three hops back against your deny list. Add the address under WATCHED ACCOUNTS and every incoming payment is screened by the server within a minute, sent to your webhooks as deposit_screened.

Something is not working. Can NOSHX fix it?

Tell NOSHX what is wrong ("it is not working, fix it") or press SELF-REPAIR in the Support panel. NOSHX checks the mainnet link and reconnects to another public server if it is dropped or silent, compares this computer's clock with the ledger's, renews an expiring sign-in, checks the NOSHASHI server, re-reads your plan, looks at your watched accounts, removes damaged saved settings, checks the help index and whether a newer version is out. It repairs what it can and says what is left and how to fix it. Say "open a ticket with this report" to send the report to support, or "post the report to NSH-1042" to add it to a ticket.

Does NOSHASHI check the OFAC sanctions list?

Yes. Every day NOSHASHI reads the US Treasury's Specially Designated Nationals list (sdn.csv and sdn_comments.csv from treasury.gov) and keeps every XRP Ledger address it names, with the entry number, name and program. Check an Address says when an address is listed, with its source; deposit screening holds a deposit whose sender, or any account that funded it up to three hops back, is listed, and never credits it; the website widget's address check shows it too. An address that is not on the list is not thereby cleared: the list names only addresses OFAC has published.

What is address poisoning and does NOSHASHI catch it?

An attacker creates an address whose first and last characters match one you use, then sends you a tiny payment so it appears in your history next to the real one, hoping you copy it into a withdrawal. Deposit screening flags any sender that starts and ends like one of your watched addresses or your trusted counterparties (set them in the deposit rules), and holds it when it arrived as dust. The website widget's VERIFY ADDRESS check tells your customers whether the address they are about to pay is really yours or a lookalike.

Can I put NOSHASHI's checks on my own website?

Yes, on Enterprise and Strategic. In ADJUDICATION › LEDGER WATCH › WEBSITE WIDGET, create a widget: choose its checks (verify that an address is really your deposit address, check any address against the ledger and the OFAC list, and deposit status by transaction hash), pick your deposit address, and list the exact sites it may appear on. Paste the two-line snippet into your page. The widget holds no key, answers only on the sites you list, and never tells a customer why a deposit is under review.

How do I make my XRP Ledger account harder to hack?

Open SECURITY CENTER › ACCOUNT CHECK (free) and enter your address, never your seed. NOSHASHI grades the account A to F from what the ledger shows: who can sign (master key, regular key, signer list and its real quorum), recent key and settings changes, address-poisoning attempts against you, and the doors strangers can use (NFT offers, checks, payment channels). The hardening plan lists unsigned transactions (for example, sign with a regular key on a hardware wallet, or require two of three signers for a treasury, and refuse unsolicited NFT offers) for you to review and sign in your own wallet. NOSHASHI never signs and never asks for a key.

My account was hacked or drained. Can I get my XRP back?

A validated XRP Ledger transaction cannot be reversed by anyone: not validators, not Ripple, not NOSHASHI, and anyone offering a paid 'recovery' is running a second scam. Do this now: move whatever is left to a new account created on a device that never held the old seed, and report it to the police (in the US, ic3.gov; in the UK, Action Fraud). Then open SECURITY CENTER › INCIDENT RESPONSE (Pro and above): it shows the key changes before the theft, follows the value hop by hop past the dust thieves spray, says where it is now, and lists the recovery paths that exist. If it reached an exchange with a destination tag, the exchange can freeze it; if it was an issued token, the issuer may freeze or claw it back. Send them the SHA-256 dossier it writes.

Can NOSHASHI alert us if one of our accounts is being taken over?

Yes, on Strategic. Watch the accounts in LEDGER WATCH; the server reads them every minute, and when one's regular key or signer list changes, its master key is disabled or re-enabled, or it is deleted, your webhooks receive a signed security_alert within a minute. A takeover almost always starts with the thief adding a key of their own, so this is the earliest warning the ledger gives. SECURITY CENTER › GUARDIAN lists these events, and INCIDENT RESPONSE can watch every account in a theft trail in one click.

Can I get an alert on my own computer if my wallet is being taken over?

Yes, free. In SECURITY CENTER › GUARDIAN, add your own addresses under PERSONAL GUARDIAN (3 on Free, 50 on Pro and above). While NOSHASHI is open it reads them every minute and raises a native notification when a new regular key or signer list appears, the master key is switched, the account is deleted, more than your threshold of XRP leaves, or a dust payment or NFT offer with a link arrives. The addresses and alerts stay on your device. For accounts that must be watched when no one has the app open, Strategic's server-side Guardian sends signed webhooks.

A website asks me to sign a transaction. How do I know what it does?

Paste it into SECURITY CENTER › PRE-SIGN CHECK (free), as JSON or as the hex blob the site shows. It is decoded on your device and explained in plain words, with a verdict: SAFE-LOOKING, CAREFUL or DO NOT SIGN. DO NOT SIGN is given for what empties accounts: a SetRegularKey or SignerListSet that hands signing to someone else, an AccountDelete, an NFT sell offer for zero, or an OFAC-listed or lookalike destination. A transaction is not a secret; a seed is, and no legitimate site ever asks for one.

Is any of my XRP stuck, and can I get my reserve back?

Open SECURITY CENTER › RECOVER FUNDS (free for one address). It reads everything the account owns and lists what comes back. That covers escrows that have matured and are waiting for someone to finish them, and expired escrows and payment channels that return to you when closed. It also covers checks written to you that you never cashed. The owner reserve (0.2 XRP each) locked by empty trust lines, old orders, NFT offers, preauthorisations and unused tickets is listed too. Each item comes with the unsigned transaction that releases it, and the scan says what AccountDelete would return if you closed the account. Pro values every other holding in XRP and scans 25 addresses at once; Institutional scans 500.

How do I revoke permissions on my XRP Ledger account?

The XRP Ledger has no token allowances, but it has standing permissions that let someone else take value: checks you wrote, NFT sell offers (a zero-price one gives the NFT away), funded payment channels, open orders, deposit preauthorisations, a regular key, signers and an authorised NFT minter. SECURITY CENTER › EXPOSURE AUDIT (free) lists every one on your account with its risk and the unsigned transaction that revokes it.

I sent XRP to an exchange and it never arrived. What happened?

Paste the transaction hash into SECURITY CENTER › DEPOSIT HELP (free). If the payment failed (for example tecDST_TAG_NEEDED), only the fee was spent and the amount is still in your account. If it succeeded without the destination tag, or with the wrong one, the funds are in the exchange's pooled account: only the exchange can credit them, and it usually will when given the facts. NOSHASHI writes that letter, with the hash, ledger, amount, tags and a SHA-256, for you to send from your logged-in account. A payment to a private wallet can only be returned by its owner.

How can I tell if an account really belongs to the company it claims?

An account's Domain field is a claim anyone can write. It is proven only when that website lists the account back in its /.well-known/xrp-ledger.toml. SECURITY CENTER › DOMAIN CHECK (free) reads the file and tells you VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED (treat it as impersonation) or that no file exists. Given a domain instead, it shows which accounts the domain vouches for and whether each names it back.

Can NOSHASHI find the other accounts a scammer uses?

Yes, on Pro and above. SECURITY CENTER › SCAM CLUSTERS starts from one known scam account. It finds who funded it, the accounts it created, and where it swept its balance when it deleted itself. It also groups accounts that share a vanity ending or a memo. Exchanges end a branch, so their customers are not pulled in, and every link names its transaction. Pro maps two hops and 40 accounts. Enterprise maps four hops and 200, and opens the report as an investigation case. Strategic watches the whole cluster server-side.

How do I get XRPL events into my own systems?

On the Strategic plan, add accounts under ADJUDICATION › LEDGER WATCH › WATCHED ACCOUNTS. The server reads each one every minute from validated ledgers and sends every event (payments, trust-line freezes, settings and issuer flag changes, clawbacks and more) to your organization's webhooks as xrpl_event, signed. You can also pull them: GET /functions/v1/noshashi-xrpl-watch/events with an organization API key, as JSON, NDJSON or CSV, cursor-paged, optionally in one of your own export schemas; POST /history backfills any ledger range.

Why did my check come back NO-GO?

NO-GO means at least one blocking rule failed, and the Verification scene names which one. In practice it is almost always one of three things: the account holds none of the XLS-70 credentials the target domain requires (most mainnet accounts hold none yet), the transfer exceeds the domain's per-settlement ceiling, or the balance does not clear the XRPL owner reserve of 1 XRP plus 0.2 XRP per owned object. Open the verdict and read the row marked BLOCK — the detail line states the exact number that failed.

What is the difference between HOLD and NO-GO?

NO-GO means a blocking rule failed and the settlement is refused. HOLD means every blocking rule passed but an advisory one did not — most often the account publishes no Domain attestation, or the target domain is under governance review. HOLD is 'a human should look at this', not 'this is forbidden'.

Why does my wallet show no credentials?

Because it genuinely holds none. XLS-70 credentials are ledger objects that an issuer creates and the subject then accepts; they do not exist until someone issues one. An empty registry on mainnet is the normal state today, not a bug or a sync failure. Any domain rule that requires a credential will correctly read NO-GO until one is issued and accepted.

The console says OFFLINE or DEGRADED.

The console holds one WebSocket to a public XRPL node and rotates across three endpoints with exponential backoff. OFFLINE almost always means outbound WebSocket traffic on port 443 is being blocked — a corporate proxy, a VPN, or a strict firewall. Run the diagnostics below and use Reconnect; if it still fails, try without the VPN.

How do I open the menu bar HUD?

Press Cmd+Shift+X from anywhere, or click the flower in the macOS menu bar. The HUD shows one thing at a glance — whether this wallet can settle right now — and the menu bar itself carries a live ticker with the gate state and current ledger height. It needs the desktop app; the browser build has no menu bar.

Where are my API keys and secrets stored?

In the macOS Keychain, through the OS keyring — never in a preferences file, never in browser storage, and never in a log. Compliance API keys you issue are stored only as a SHA-256 hash, shown once at creation, and cannot be recovered afterwards by you or by us. Model-provider keys are scoped per provider so revoking one does not disturb another.

Account → Manage Billing opens Stripe's own portal; cancelling takes two clicks, needs no email and no phone call, and access continues to the end of the period you already paid for. Full refund within 14 days of a first subscription charge if you have not used a paid capability, and unused verification credits are refundable pro rata within 30 days.

What does the Authority Certificate screen do?

Authority Certificate: what authority an issuer has kept over an asset it issued — whether it can freeze a holder, whether it gave that power up irrevocably (lsfNoFreeze cannot be cleared once set), whether the asset is frozen right now, whether holding it needs the issuer's permission, whether one signer reaches the quorum alone, what it charges on a transfer between holders, and how concentrated the supply is. Each answer is a fact at one named ledger index, and the set is digested with SHA-256 so the same reading can be checked again later. It is NOT a score — no number is composited from the checks — and NOT a legal finding: whether an asset is decentralised or is a security is a determination for an agency applying statutory criteria, which this software does not evaluate. If the supply walk is skipped, or trust-line coverage falls below 95%, the concentration check abstains rather than passing. It needs the Desk plan.

Enter an XRP Ledger issuing account. NOSHASHI reads validated ledger state and reports the authority that issuer has kept over the asset it issues — whether it can freeze you, whether it gave that power up for good, whether one key signs for it, and how concentrated the supply is. WHAT THIS IS NOT It is not a score. There is no number out of a hundred and no grade. Seven questions are answered separately and left separate, because a composite invites an argument about the composite instead of about the facts underneath it. It is not a legal finding. Whether a digital asset is “decentralised”, or is a security, is a determination for the SEC and the CFTC applying statutory criteria. This reports ledger facts that bear on that question. It does not answer it, and nothing here should be quoted as though it did. WHEN IT REFUSES TO ANSWER If a read fails, the certificate says so and fails — it never returns a clean result because a request timed out. THE DIGEST Every certificate carries a SHA-256 digest over the verdict, the issuer, the currency it was scoped to, the ledger index , where the holder distribution was read from , the version of the rule set that decided it and every check with its result. The ledger index is inside the digest deliberately: the same issuer at a later ledger is a different assertion and does not share this one. Keep the digest and the reading can be shown to be the reading that was taken, months later, by anyone holding it. The rule-set version is in there because the checks can be tightened. Two certificates can carry the same issuer, the same ledger and the same results and still be different claims, if the thresholds those results were decided against moved between them. Binding the version keeps the older reading readable instead of quietly reinterpreted under rules it was never evaluated against.

NOSHX's own language model is trained from NOSHASHI's own content with the free kit in scripts/noshx-model . What does NOSHASHI's AI docs say about Support tickets?

Signed-in customers open a ticket from NOSHX › TICKETS › NEW TICKET, with a subject, a topic, a priority and a description, and optionally the app version and platform. Each ticket gets a reference such as NSH-1042. NOSHASHI support replies in the same thread; the customer is emailed about a reply, and support is emailed about a new ticket or a customer's reply. A ticket reads WAITING ON SUPPORT until support answers, then SUPPORT REPLIED; either side can mark it RESOLVED, and a customer's reply reopens it.
Tickets are held in NOSHASHI's database with row level security: a customer can read only their own tickets, and only support staff can read every ticket. Messages cannot be edited or deleted by anyone. Every write goes through a server function that checks who is writing, and a ticket or reply containing an XRPL secret seed is refused in the app before it is sent. At most 10 tickets a day can be opened from one account.

Check results: five states: what should I know? (from the API docs)

Every check carries passed , and may carry state : PASS , FAIL , REVIEW , INSUFFICIENT_DATA or NOT_APPLICABLE . Without state , the state is implied: PASS when passed, otherwise FAIL for a blocking check and REVIEW for an advisory one.
INSUFFICIENT_DATA ( passed: false ) means the evidence the rule needs could not be read. It is no answer, not a failure.
NOT_APPLICABLE ( passed: true ) means the rule does not apply to this subject, for example supply concentration for an issuer with nothing outstanding.
In a digest a check is [id, passed] , or [id, passed, state] when the state is one of those two. Every receipt and certificate issued before the states existed therefore keeps its bytes. authority/check accepts state on each check and binds it the same way; any other value is refused with invalid_checks .

Regulator seats: what should I know? (from the Enterprise docs)

An owner, admin or compliance member can give an examiner a read-only seat for 1 to 180 days (Institutional and above). The examiner signs in with their own NOSHASHI account and reads the organization's policies, exceptions, investigations and audit log; every write the server offers refuses them. The seat stops working at its end date without anyone acting, because membership itself honours the expiry, and each visit is written to the audit log (at most once every 30 minutes). Granting, extending and revoking a seat are audit entries too.

Explain Deposit screening (Enterprise), as NOSHASHI's Enterprise docs describes it.

ADJUDICATION › LEDGER WATCH screens an incoming payment before it is credited, read live from the ledger. It credits what actually arrived ( delivered_amount ; a partial payment that asks for 100,000 XRP and delivers 0.077 is credited 0.077), holds a familiar ticker whose issuer owes nothing as counterfeit, flags a drop of dust whose memo carries a link as a phishing lure, notes a missing destination tag, the issuer's freeze and clawback rights and your Travel Rule threshold, and reads who created the sender, who created them and who created them, checking all three against the organization's deny list. The verdict is clear, review or hold, with the amount to credit; a fact that could not be read holds the deposit rather than passing it. Watched deposit addresses are screened by the server every minute, without the app open.

Tell me about XRPL event feeds (Strategic) in NOSHASHI.

An organization can watch up to 100 accounts. The server reads each one's new validated transactions every minute and records payments, trust-line freezes and changes, account settings and issuer flag changes, offers, checks, escrows, clawbacks, NFT and AMM activity; another party's trade that only rippled through the account is recorded as such, not as the account's own act. Verdicts: what should I know? (from the Policies docs)

Verdict | Meaning |
GO | Every blocking rule passed. Settlement is cleared to broadcast. |
HOLD | Blocking rules passed but an advisory rule failed. Manual sign-off required. |
NO-GO | A blocking rule failed. Settlement is refused by the compliance layer. |
INSUFFICIENT DATA | A rule could not be evaluated because the evidence it needs could not be read. This is not a pass, a failure or a soft refusal — it is the absence of an answer, and it says nothing about the subject. |
A blocking failure gives NO-GO. Otherwise an evidence source that could not be read gives INSUFFICIENT DATA. Otherwise an advisory failure gives HOLD. Otherwise GO.

1.0.10: what should I know? (from the Release notes docs)

Model requests are now made by the app itself rather than its window. A provider key goes from the operating system keyring straight to that provider's own host; the window can store, check or clear a key but not read one back. A named provider's key is only ever sent to that provider, a custom endpoint must use HTTPS, and local models never receive a key. NOSHX Core: its own engine, no outside model NOSHX now runs on NOSHX Core by default: NOSHASHI's own engine, with no language model at all. It works out what is being asked (addresses, transaction hashes, currency codes, and what you want to know about them), runs the matching ledger readers, and writes the answer from what it read, in the same words the screens use. Product and compliance questions are answered with the most relevant sentences from NOSHASHI's pages, with their sources, and "which screen" questions name the screens that fit and the plan each needs. It answers in milliseconds, works offline, needs nothing installed and runs on any laptop.

LEDGER CADENCE reported a healthy network as failing. 0.3.0 measured the interval between closes by differencing ledger_time , which is not a timestamp of the resolution that implies: XRPL rounds a close time to the ledger's close_time_resolution , and when the rounded value collides with the parent's it takes parent + 1 second instead. Consecutive closes inside one resolution bucket therefore report exactly 1s, and the bucket boundary reports 8s or 9s. Measured against mainnet on 2026-09-15, thirty-three consecutive intervals read 9,1,1,8,1,1,8 — never once the three to four seconds the network actually runs at. Their mean was 3.94s, which is right, because the rounding preserves the total and destroys the distribution. Drawn per-interval it announced eighteen of twenty-eight closes as out of band while the network was entirely healthy — the panel inventing a fault, which is the one thing this product is sold on not doing.

LedgerStreamClose.closeAt is the ledger's own close time in epoch millis — deliberately not the moment the frame arrived here, because arrival interval measures this machine's connection and a local network stall would otherwise render as XRPL slowing down. It is zero rather than a date when a node omits ledger_time , since rippleTimeToDate(0) is 2000-01-01 and differencing against it would manufacture an interval. Two things in COMPLIANCE COVERAGE were drawn as measurements that were not measurements. DOMAIN ENFORCEMENT was connected ? 100 : 0 and NODE LOAD FACTOR was 100 / loadFactor , both rendered as percentage bars. A bar implies a scale and a measured position on it; a binary has no such continuum, and an inverted multiplier is not a percentage of anything. Both are now states, showing the actual load multiplier and distinguishing "not read" from "off" — a node that never reported a load factor is not a node under no load.

Tell me about Delivery and retries in NOSHASHI.

Deliveries leave the database after the transaction that recorded the event commits; nothing is sent for an action that was rolled back. A 2xx response marks the delivery delivered. Anything else, a timeout (10 s) or no response is recorded as failed and retried, up to three attempts in all: the second about a minute after the first fails, the third about four minutes after the second. Each attempt carries a fresh timestamp and signature and the same delivery id. Delivery history is visible to owners and admins in the app.

Explain 1 · What the XRP Ledger is, as NOSHASHI's A plain guide to the XRP Ledger and what NOSHASHI does describes it.

The XRP Ledger is a shared public record of who holds what. Around every four
seconds it agrees on a new version of that record — a ledger —
and once agreed, it never changes. Anyone can read it. Nobody needs permission.
PUT ANOTHER WAY
Think of a bank statement that the whole world can read, that updates every
four seconds, and that no single bank controls. That is roughly it.
The live numbers on our front page are read straight from that record, over a
public connection, at the moment you load the page. Nothing is cached or invented.

2 · Who really owns a token: what should I know? (from the A plain guide to the XRP Ledger and what NOSHASHI does)

XRP itself is the ledger's own currency and belongs to whoever holds it. But most
things on the ledger are not XRP — they are issued currencies : a
dollar, a euro, or a token that some company has put onto the ledger.
An issued token is closer to an IOU than to cash. A company called the
issuer promises it is worth something, and the ledger records who
holds how much of that promise.
WHY THIS MATTERS
Cash in your pocket is yours. A gift card is a promise from a shop — and the shop
has more say over it than you do. Most tokens are gift cards, not cash.

Tell me about 3 · Freeze rights — the part almost nobody checks in NOSHASHI.

The issuer of a token can usually freeze it. That is a real, built-in
power of the ledger, not a loophole. When an issuer freezes, the holder can no longer
send or redeem what they hold. The balance still shows in the wallet. It just cannot move.
There is a stronger version, called deep freeze , which also stops the
holder receiving . The difference matters: an ordinary freeze aimed at a
sanctioned address still lets that address keep accepting money.
Some issuers permanently give up this power. That is published on the ledger too, as a
flag called lsfNoFreeze , and once set it can never be undone.
An issuer that has set it can never freeze you.
WHAT NOSHASHI READS
For every token you hold, we read the issuer's flags and tell you plainly: can this
issuer freeze you, have they already, have they given up the right, and do they charge
a fee every time the token moves. Most wallets show you a balance and nothing else.

Tell me about 4 · Why "it's worth $X" can be false in NOSHASHI.

The ledger has a built-in marketplace. People post offers — "I will buy 500 of this at
this price" — and the collection of those offers is the order book .
A price is only real if somebody will actually trade at it. If the best offer is for
five dollars' worth, then the "price" describes five dollars, not your whole holding.
Selling more means walking down to worse and worse offers.
A CONCRETE EXAMPLE, MEASURED ON THE REAL LEDGER
One book appeared to hold 12.7 million dollars of buyers. Once we
excluded offers priced so far from the market that nobody would ever fill them, the
genuinely reachable amount was 13,894 dollars — about 913 times less.
That gap is not fraud. It is just what a raw order book looks like when nobody filters
it. But if you valued a position on the first number, you would be badly wrong.

Explain 5 · What an amendment is, as NOSHASHI's A plain guide to the XRP Ledger and what NOSHASHI does describes it.

The XRP Ledger changes slowly and in public. A proposed change is written up as a
numbered document — you will see these as XLS-70 ,
XLS-80 and so on — and then it has to be
voted in by the servers that run the network.
A feature therefore exists in three different states, and they are easy to confuse:
State | |
Specified | Somebody has written the document. Nothing works yet. |
Implemented | The server software understands it. Still nothing works on the live network. |
Activated | Enough of the network voted it in. Now it works. |
Software that checks only the second state will happily offer you a feature that every
server on the network will reject. NOSHASHI checks the third — it asks the live ledger
which amendments are actually switched on, and hides anything that is not.
ACTIVATED TODAY, AND USED BY NOSHASHI
XLS-70 | Credentials — a verifiable statement about an account, issued by somebody else. |
XLS-80 | Permissioned domains — a walled garden where only accounts holding the right credentials may trade. |
XLS-81 | Permissioned order books — a members-only marketplace. |
XLS-77 | Deep freeze — blocks sending and receiving. |
XLS-85 | Token escrow — hold any token in escrow, not just XRP. |
Some things people expect — on-ledger lending and confidential transfers — are written
and built but not yet voted in . We do not offer them, and we say so.

Explain 6 · What NOSHASHI actually does, as NOSHASHI's A plain guide to the XRP Ledger and what NOSHASHI does describes it.

Before you move anything, NOSHASHI answers two questions at once, from the same
four-second-old copy of the ledger:
Am I allowed to move this? Checked against the rules of wherever it is going.
Could I actually get out of it? Checked against the real order book and pool.
It answers with one of three words, and always tells you which rule decided it:
GO Every rule you configured passed.
HOLD Something advisory failed. A person should look before continuing.
NO-GO A blocking rule failed. The settlement is refused.
Nothing is signed and nothing is sent. It is a check you run before a transaction
exists, which is exactly why it can be run at all — it costs no fee and risks nothing.
Every answer comes with a receipt: a fingerprint of the check, computed the same way every
time. Two people running the same check get the same fingerprint, which is what makes it
worth handing to an auditor.

▶ Watch video 2: XRP Ledger basics (2:35)
The XRP Ledger (XRPL) is a public database, run since 2012, that keeps one shared record of who owns what. Thousands of servers around the world keep identical copies. Anyone can read it. Nobody, including its creators, can quietly change it.

Explain Ledgers, one after another, as NOSHASHI's Learn course describes it.

The record moves forward in steps. Every 3 to 5 seconds the network produces a new ledger : a complete snapshot of every account and balance, plus the transactions that changed things since the last one. Each ledger has a number, its ledger index , which only ever goes up. At the time of writing it is past 107 million.
Ledger 107,207,970 → 3–5 s → Ledger 107,207,971 → 3–5 s → Ledger 107,207,972

What does NOSHASHI's Learn course say about Consensus: how strangers agree?

There is no mining. Instead, special servers called validators compare the transactions they have seen and vote. Each server trusts a list of validators it believes will not collude, called its UNL (Unique Node List). When at least 80% of trusted validators agree on the same set of transactions, that ledger becomes a validated ledger . From that moment it is final: it cannot be reversed or edited.
Ledgers exist in three states:
Open / current : the ledger still collecting transactions. Its contents can change.
Closed : no more transactions, but not yet agreed.
Validated : agreed and final. This is the only kind NOSHASHI reads.
THINK OF IT LIKE
A notebook that thousands of accountants keep at once. Every few seconds they compare their newest page. When 80% of the ones you trust have written the same page, it is glued into the book forever and given a page number.

What does NOSHASHI's Learn course say about Keys?

Control of an account comes from a secret key. The secret (or seed, usually starting with s ) generates a key pair: the private key signs transactions, the public key lets everyone check the signature. Anyone with the secret controls the account completely, so it must never be shared. NOSHASHI never asks for one: it only reads public data.

Explain Reserves, as NOSHASHI's Learn course describes it.

To stop people filling the shared ledger with junk, every account must keep some XRP locked as a reserve : a base reserve to exist (currently 1 XRP) plus an owner reserve for each object it owns, such as a trust line or an offer (currently 0.2 XRP each). Validators can vote to change these amounts. Reserved XRP cannot be spent, which is why NOSHASHI distinguishes a balance from what is actually spendable .

What an account records: what should I know? (from the Learn course)

FIELD | WHAT IT HOLDS |
Balance | Its XRP, in drops (1 XRP = 1,000,000 drops). |
Sequence | A counter that goes up with each transaction; starts at the ledger index when the account was created, not at zero. |
Flags | On/off settings, including the issuer powers in lesson 5. |
OwnerCount | How many objects it owns, which sets its owner reserve. |
RegularKey | An optional second key (lesson 6). |
Domain | An optional web domain the owner claims; can be verified against a file on that domain. |
TransferRate | For issuers, the fee charged when holders transfer its tokens (lesson 5). |
A COMMON MISREADING
An account's Sequence is not how many transactions it has made. It starts at the ledger index of the account's creation. NOSHASHI's Provenance screen corrects for this when it estimates account age.
KEY IDEA Whoever holds the key owns the account. Balance minus reserve is what can actually move.

Every change to the ledger is a transaction : a signed instruction such as Payment, OfferCreate (place a trade), TrustSet (open a trust line) or AccountSet (change a setting). What does NOSHASHI's Learn course say about Life of a transaction?

The owner signs it with their key and submits it to a server.
The server gives a tentative result. This is not final.
Validators include it in a ledger that becomes validated.
Its final result is now fixed in the transaction's metadata.

Tell me about Trust lines in NOSHASHI.

Explain Currency codes do not prove anything, as NOSHASHI's Learn course describes it.

A token is identified by two things together: its currency code (a 3-character code like USD , or a 40-character hex code for longer names) and its issuer address. Tell me about How much is out there in NOSHASHI.

An issuer's obligations are the total of its tokens held by others, readable with the gateway_balances call. That is the real circulating supply per currency, and it is what NOSHASHI reports as outstanding.
THINK OF IT LIKE
A gift card. It is only worth something because the shop that issued it promises to honour it, and the shop printed the rules on the back. A card with the same name from a different shop is a different card.

Explain 5 · What an issuer can still do to your tokens, as NOSHASHI's Learn course describes it.

ABOUT 8 MINUTES · THE MOST IMPORTANT LESSON
▶ Watch video 3: What an issuer can still do to your tokens (2:49)
Issuers can turn on powers, stored as flags on their account and settings on each trust line. They are public, but almost no wallet shows them. They decide whether a token is really yours.
POWER | LEDGER NAME | WHAT IT MEANS FOR A HOLDER |
Individual freeze | lsfLowFreeze / lsfHighFreeze | The issuer freezes one holder's trust line. That holder can only send the token back to the issuer. |
Global freeze | lsfGlobalFreeze | Every holder is frozen at once; the token stops moving for everyone except back to the issuer. |
Deep freeze | Deep Freeze amendment (XLS-77) | A frozen holder can neither send nor receive the token, closing gaps the older freeze left. |
No Freeze | lsfNoFreeze | The issuer permanently gives up freezing. It can never be switched back off. |
Require Auth | lsfRequireAuth | You need the issuer's approval before you can hold the token. Used by regulated issuers. |
Clawback | lsfAllowTrustLineClawback | The issuer can take tokens back out of your account. It can only be switched on before the issuer has any trust lines, so it is permanent for that token. |
Transfer fee | TransferRate | A percentage (0% to 100%) charged each time holders send the token to each other. The issuer can change it. |

ABOUT 6 MINUTES
An account can be signed for in three ways, and more than one can be active at once:
Master key : the original key pair. It can be disabled with lsfDisableMaster , but only if another way to sign exists.
Regular key : a second key the account nominates. Useful for keeping the master key offline; it can be changed or removed.
Signer list (multi-signature): up to 32 signers, each with a weight . A transaction is valid when the weights of those who signed add up to the quorum .

Weights: Alice 3, Bob 2, Carol 2, Dan 1, Eve 1. Quorum: 5.

The XRPL has had a built-in exchange, the DEX , since 2012. Anyone can post an offer with OfferCreate, for example "sell 100 USD.Bitstamp for 190 XRP". All offers for one pair form an order book : bids on one side, asks on the other. When a new offer matches an existing one, they cross and trade. Token-to-token trades can be auto-bridged through XRP when that gives a better price.

Tell me about Listed depth versus funded depth in NOSHASHI.

Here is the catch that most tools miss. An offer stays on the book even after its owner no longer has the funds to fill it. It is still listed, but it cannot trade. These are unfunded offers . So:
Listed depth = everything shown on the book.
Funded depth = only what owners can actually deliver.
The ledger reports this itself. When you ask a server for a book with book_offers , an offer whose owner cannot cover it comes back with an extra field, taker_gets_funded , showing how much they really have. Adding up the listed amounts overstates the market.
WORKED EXAMPLE
Three offers to sell a token, each listing 10,000. The first owner holds 10,000, the second 500, the third 0. Listed depth: 30,000. Funded depth: 10,500. If you tried to sell 20,000 into this book, most of it would not fill.

Tell me about 8 · AMM pools in NOSHASHI.

ABOUT 5 MINUTES
Since the AMM amendment ( XLS-30 ), the XRPL also has automated market makers : pools that hold two assets, for example XRP and a stablecoin, and trade against anyone at a price set by the ratio of the two balances. The DEX routes trades through both order books and pools, whichever is better.
Liquidity providers deposit both assets and receive LP tokens , a share of the pool.
Every swap pays a trading fee (up to 1%) that goes to the pool. LP token holders vote on the fee, weighted by how many LP tokens they hold.
The auction slot is a seat anyone can bid LP tokens for. Its holder trades at a heavily discounted fee for a period, which rewards active traders who keep the pool's price in line.
A pool whose asset is frozen by its issuer can be frozen too.
NOSHASHI's Pool Governance screen shows who votes the fee, what share of LP tokens those votes represent, and who holds the auction slot, because a pool whose fee is set by one large holder behaves differently from one with a spread of voters.
KEY IDEA A pool's fee and discounts are governed by whoever holds the most LP tokens. Check who that is.

What does NOSHASHI's Learn course say about Partial payments?

A Payment's Amount field says how much should arrive. But if the sender sets the partial payment flag ( tfPartialPayment ), the Amount becomes only a maximum . The payment can deliver far less and still finish with tesSUCCESS .
The authoritative figure is delivered_amount in the transaction's metadata. The XRPL's own documentation tells applications to credit that. Exchanges that credited Amount instead have been drained: attackers sent "large" payments that delivered almost nothing and withdrew the difference.

Explain 10 · NFTs and the rights issuers keep, as NOSHASHI's Learn course describes it.

ABOUT 4 MINUTES
The XRPL supports native NFTs (non-fungible tokens, XLS-20): unique tokens for art, tickets, deeds or memberships. Each one has a 64-character NFTokenID , and the ID itself encodes the rules the issuer set when minting:
Burnable : the issuer can destroy it, even while you own it.
Transferable : if not set, you can only sell it back to the issuer.
Only XRP : it can only be sold for XRP.
Mutable : the issuer can change what its URI points at, so the picture or document can change after you buy it.
Transfer fee : the issuer takes up to 50% of every resale.
Because these rules are inside the ID, NOSHASHI's Token Rights screen can decode them without even contacting the ledger.
KEY IDEA Owning an NFT does not mean the issuer is done with it. Its ID tells you what they kept.

Explain 11 · Amendments: how the rules change, as NOSHASHI's Learn course describes it.

ABOUT 4 MINUTES
The XRPL's rules are changed by amendments . A new feature is written into the server software, then validators vote. It switches on only when it keeps at least 80% support for two weeks in a row. Servers that have not upgraded when an amendment activates become amendment blocked and stop following the ledger.
Many features in this course arrived this way: AMM (XLS-30), Clawback (XLS-39), NFTs (XLS-20), Credentials (XLS-70), Permissioned Domains (XLS-80) and Deep Freeze (XLS-77). "XLS" numbers are the public proposals behind them. NOSHASHI's Domain Grid lists which amendments are enabled.
KEY IDEA New rules need a supermajority for two weeks. What is enabled today is readable from the ledger.

What does NOSHASHI's Learn course say about 14 · How NOSHASHI reads the ledger?

ABOUT 5 MINUTES
Validated only. It reads validated ledgers from mainnet, the real XRP Ledger. Nothing is estimated, simulated or backfilled.
Four servers, compared. It queries four public servers by name. If they disagree, the disagreement is shown as a finding, never averaged away.
It says when it cannot tell. Where a figure cannot be established (for example, too little of a supply could be read to measure concentration), the app withholds it and says so, instead of showing zero.
No keys, no custody. It never asks for a secret key, never signs, never moves money. It only reads public data.
Stamped and fingerprinted. Every result carries the ledger index it was read at and a SHA-256 digest : a fingerprint of the exact result. Change one character and the digest changes completely.
Local first. Your adjudication history (up to 10,000 verdicts) is stored on your device. The AI agent runs on your device by default.
Self-verifying. The app can hash its own program file, so you can confirm you are running the published build.
The calls it makes are standard XRPL server methods, listed in Under the hood , so anyone can reproduce a reading with their own tools.

Explain 16 · Verdicts, checks and receipts, as NOSHASHI's Learn course describes it.

ABOUT 6 MINUTES
When NOSHASHI adjudicates something, it runs a set of checks , each with a severity. The overall verdict follows from them:
GO Every check passed. Nothing on the ledger stands in the way.
HOLD A warning-level check did not pass, or a check needs review. A person should look before moving.
NO-GO A blocking check failed. Do not move until it is resolved or formally excepted.
Each individual check reports one of five states:
PASS Run and satisfied.
FAIL Run and not satisfied.
REVIEW Needs a human decision.
INSUFFICIENT_DATA The ledger did not give enough to decide. An abstention, never a pass.
NOT_APPLICABLE The check does not apply here.

What does NOSHASHI's Learn course say about 20 · Account security: making an account hard to take over?

ABOUT 7 MINUTES
An XRP Ledger account belongs to whoever can sign for it. Nobody at a help desk can reset it, and no transaction can be undone. So security on the XRPL is about one question: who holds a key that can sign, and how easily could someone else get it?
Most accounts are emptied the same way: the secret seed is exposed. It gets typed into a fake wallet or "airdrop claim" site, stored in a cloud note or screenshot, or read off the clipboard by malware. The ledger itself is not broken into.

Tell me about The four defences, from simplest to strongest in NOSHASHI.

Keep the master seed offline. Write it on paper or steel, never in a photo, email or cloud note. Nobody legitimate, including NOSHASHI, ever needs it.
Sign with a regular key held in a hardware wallet ( SetRegularKey ). Day-to-day signing never touches the master seed. If the regular key leaks, the master key replaces it in one transaction.
Require several signers for a treasury ( SignerListSet , for example two of three). One stolen seed can then move nothing. Then disable the master key, or the signer list can be bypassed.
Close the doors strangers use. AccountSet flags can refuse unsolicited NFT offers, checks and payment channels, which is how many phishing links arrive. Deposit Authorisation goes further: only senders you approve can pay you at all.

What does NOSHASHI's Learn course say about Address poisoning?

Wallets show only the first and last few characters of an address. An attacker generates an address whose start and end match one you pay, then sends you a tiny amount so the fake sits in your history right next to the real one. The next time you copy "the usual" address from history, you pay the attacker.
A REAL EXAMPLE, RECORDED FROM MAINNET
The account rfWPjcbY5QT2shRFY2SSQHFKPYSMzxaMaN sent 1-drop payments (0.000001 XRP) with a memo offering a "free XRP gift" at a fake Xaman site. It then swept its balance by AccountDelete into rDS6r59hQ3X95a2jeguAdTRMvC3b5xaMan , which did the same into r3LQQNg7hEdbbNK3w4ykfLRDQWAc7xAmAn , and so on. Every one of them was generated to end in "xaman", the name of a real wallet.

What to do in the first hour: what should I know? (from the Learn course)

Move anything left to a brand-new account created on a device that never held the old seed. Whoever has the old key can empty the rest at any moment.

Tell me about The recovery paths that do exist in NOSHASHI.

A custodial service freezes a deposit. If stolen value was paid to an exchange (an account that requires destination tags), the exchange can identify and freeze the customer behind that tag if reached quickly, usually with a police reference.
A token's issuer freezes or claws back. Issued tokens are the issuer's obligations. Unless it has given up the right, the issuer can freeze the trust lines holding stolen tokens, and with clawback enabled it can take them back and reissue them.
Sanctions and law enforcement. If the trail reaches a listed address (OFAC SDN), authorities have powers individuals do not.

What does NOSHASHI's Learn course say about XRP you can get back?

Matured escrows. An escrow does not pay out on its own. Once its FinishAfter time passes, someone must submit EscrowFinish , or the XRP waits forever.
Expired escrows and payment channels. After CancelAfter or an expiry, EscrowCancel or a closing PaymentChannelClaim returns what was never paid out, plus the reserve.
Uncashed checks. A check written to you pays nothing until you submit CheckCash .
The owner reserve. Every object an account owns locks 0.2 XRP: each trust line, DEX order, NFT offer, ticket and preauthorisation. Removing ones you no longer need frees it. Closing an account entirely with AccountDelete returns everything except a 0.2 XRP fee.
REAL EXAMPLES, RECORDED FROM MAINNET TODAY

A protection fund no single key can move: what should I know? (from the Learn course)

An institution can also set XRP aside to make customers whole up to a limit each, the way a deposit scheme promises a fixed amount per depositor. The ledger shows whether that fund is real:
locked in escrow until a date: nobody can move it early;
under a signer list with the master key disabled: several people must sign;
behind one key : whoever holds it can take it, so it counts for nothing.
Ripple's escrow wallet #03 shows the strongest form: 3.3 billion XRP locked in escrows, the account itself under a 4-of-8 signer list.
This is verification, not insurance. NOSHASHI pays no claims, and no government scheme stands behind a program. It shows what is really set aside.

What does NOSHASHI's Learn course say about Stopping XRP leaving to the wrong place?

Withdrawal screening checks a customer's withdrawal before it is signed: whether it will bounce, whether the destination is brand new or hours old (most stolen withdrawals go to fresh accounts), whether it imitates an address the customer used before, and whether it or its funders are OFAC-listed or reported scams.
The shared scam registry holds addresses institutions reported with transaction evidence, each confirmed by a reviewer who did not file it.
The phishing link feed reads a validated ledger every minute and keeps every domain advertised in XRP dust. A real relay sprayed 1-drop payments at 99 accounts, then deleted itself into the next account.
The emergency kit is the ordered set of transactions that saves a compromised account: take back what others can pull, move the value to a cold account, change the keys. Built on tickets, it can be signed today and kept offline.
Market surveillance reads a token's order-book history: one account placed and replaced 171 EUROP orders in minutes and none filled. That makes a book look deeper than it is, whether it is spoofing or an ordinary market maker re-quoting.

Explain Questions people ask, as NOSHASHI's Learn course describes it.

Do I need to own crypto or connect a wallet?
No. NOSHASHI only reads public ledger data. It never asks for a secret key and cannot move funds.
Does a GO mean something is safe?
No. GO means nothing on the ledger stands in the way under the checks that ran. It says nothing about the business behind an issuer, prices or the future.
Why is a well-known issuer NO-GO?
Usually because one key can sign for it, or it keeps freeze rights. Those are normal for many regulated issuers. The verdict states the fact so you decide knowingly; it is not an accusation.
Why does a figure say "insufficient data" instead of a number?
Because the ledger did not return enough to support one. NOSHASHI will not guess and will not show zero for "unknown".
Can I check a reading myself?
Yes. Ask any XRPL server for the same data at the same ledger index, or re-run the free certificate. Recomputing the digest over the same contents gives the same value.
Where is my data stored?
Your verdict history and the local agent stay on your device. Account, plan and organisation features use the NOSHASHI service. The website certificate stores nothing.
Is this financial or legal advice?
No. It reports ledger facts and what they imply. Decisions remain yours and your advisers'.

FOR THE CURIOUS How NOSHASHI is built The desktop app uses Tauri 2: a Rust core with a React and TypeScript interface, packaged natively for macOS, Windows and Linux, with an iOS build in progress. It connects to public XRPL servers directly over WebSocket and compares four of them. Accounts, plans and organisation features (policies, exceptions, investigations, webhooks, the Compliance API) run on Supabase edge functions with row-level security. This website is a static site on Vercel with a few server functions, such as the free certificate. Releases are built by GitHub Actions and signed, and installed copies update themselves. The ledger calls it uses ledger : the latest validated ledger index. account_info : an account's balance, flags, sequence and regular key. account_objects : signer lists, escrows, offers and other owned objects. account_lines : trust lines, limits, balances and freeze state. gateway_balances : an issuer's obligations per currency. book_offers : order books, including taker_gets_funded . amm_info : pool balances, fee, votes and auction slot.

tx and account_tx : transactions and their metadata, including delivered_amount . How the authority verdict is computed Six checks: freeze permanently surrendered (warning), issuance not globally frozen now (blocking), holding does not require issuer permission (warning), no single key controls the issuer (blocking), no issuer transfer fee (warning), and supply concentration (warning; an abstention when the supply was not walked). Any failed blocking check gives NO-GO; otherwise any failed warning gives HOLD; otherwise GO. The certificate records the ledger index, the rules version and a SHA-256 digest over the canonical checks. terminals read the book and never look at who can freeze the balance. A desk
holding an issued asset has to answer both — am I allowed to move this ,
and could I actually get out of it — and answering them from two systems
at two moments produces a position that looks fine in each and is not.
NOSHASHI reads both sides of the same validated ledger state, in the same second,
and reconciles them into one verdict.
All plans read XRPL Mainnet. There is no testnet mode, because a compliance
answer about a test network is not an answer.

Every verdict follows this path. Open a stage to see what happens there and where it is implemented. 01 XRPL MAINNET Public XRP Ledger servers, read over WebSocket and HTTPS. The app connects directly to public servers: xrplcluster.com, s1.ripple.com and s2.ripple.com, in failover order (the Network view also compares xrpl.ws). The Compliance API reads s1 and s2 over HTTPS. No NOSHASHI server sits between the app and the ledger. Only read commands are sent; the full list is below and is checked by test. Source: src/lib/xrpl/link.ts · src/lib/xrpl/client.ts 02 VALIDATED STATE Ledger state is read from the last validated ledger, never an open one. Every state read asks for ledger_index "validated" or reads a validated range. A transaction counts as final only when the server says validated: true; until then it is shown as not final. The default is a model on your own machine, and the app shows which applies. | 04 / Human oversight A policy submitted by one member must be activated by another; the server refuses self-activation. Policy exceptions are requested by one member and decided by another, and every decision is written to an append-only audit log. Investigations are opened, prioritised and closed by people. The AI assistant can be asked about a case but cannot create, change or close one. Every call to an AI model is recorded with digests and sizes, so what was sent and when can be shown without keeping a second copy of the text. 05 / What this page does not claim NOSHASHI trusts the public servers it reads from. It does not verify ledger proofs or validator signatures itself, and individual reads are not cross-checked between servers (the Network view compares servers separately). A receipt digest shows the receipt was not altered. It is not a signature and does not by itself prove NOSHASHI issued it.
